title: Batch Mode Sends Full Files
body: **Batch Mode Sends Full Files** When one file has two or more fixable issues, the batch fix path builds a prompt from the sanitized full file and only falls back if the estimated token budget is exceeded. A large file can therefore be sent in full, even though this section says files over 500 lines use only a context window.

title: Prompt Budget Is Best Effort
body: **Prompt Budget Is Best Effort** `max_prompt_tokens` is not a hard cap in all fix paths. The single-issue path can still send the 3-line minimum window after it remains over budget, and refinement prompts do not apply the same shrinking loop, so this can understate how much code may leave the environment.

title: Transport Is Not Enforced
body: **Transport Is Not Enforced** The normal config path accepts `ai.enabled: true` without `transport`, and provider selection falls back to API transport when it is unset. Users following this reference may expect a missing transport to fail fast, but fix/check flows can instead run with the API transport unless they separately run the diagnostic command.

title: Transport not enforced
body: **Transport not enforced** This still says `transport` is required when `enabled: true`, but the normal check/fix path accepts config with no `transport` and provider creation falls back to API transport. When a user enables AI without this field, the run can silently use API transport or fail with a less useful availability error instead of failing fast on the missing setting.

title: Batch sends full files
body: **Batch sends full files** This size-based rule only describes the single-issue fix path. When one file has multiple fixable issues, the batch fix path builds its prompt from the sanitized full file and only falls back if the estimated prompt is over `max_prompt_tokens`. A file over 500 lines can still be sent in full when that estimate fits, so this section still understates what code may leave the environment.

title: Budget is best effort
body: **Budget is best effort** This presents `max_prompt_tokens` as a cap in all cases, but some fix paths can exceed it. The single-issue path sends the 3-line minimum window even when it is still over budget, and refinement prompts do not use the same shrinking check before being sent. Very wide lines or refinement retries can therefore send more code than this section promises.

title: Transport Not Enforced
body: **Transport Not Enforced** This still describes `transport` as required for enabled AI, but normal check and fix runs can load `ai.enabled: true` without it and then fall back to API transport during provider creation. A user who expects a missing `transport` to fail fast can instead run with an implicit API transport or hit a later provider error. Please document the actual fallback behavior or make the normal runtime path enforce this requirement. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

title: Batch Sends Full Files
body: **Batch Sends Full Files** This size rule does not cover the batch fix path. When one file has multiple fixable issues, batch prompt construction embeds the sanitized full file and only falls back to per-issue prompts when the estimated prompt is over `max_prompt_tokens`. A file over 500 lines can still be sent in full when that estimate fits, even though this text says larger files use only a context window.

title: Budget Is Best Effort
body: **Budget Is Best Effort** This still presents `max_prompt_tokens` as a hard cap for every fix-mode prompt, but some paths can exceed or skip that cap. The single-issue path can send the 3-line minimum window even when it remains over budget, and refinement prompts build a fixed context window without the same shrinking check. Very wide lines or refinement retries can therefore send more code than this section promises.

title: Transport Fallback Overstated
body: **Transport Fallback Overstated** This still describes the missing-`transport` behavior too broadly. Anthropic and OpenAI check/fix runs can fall back to API transport, but diagnostics report a missing `ai.transport` value as incompatible, and `provider: cursor` resolves the missing value to API before rejecting it because Cursor only supports CLI transport. A user can follow this reference, omit `transport`, and then get either a diagnostics failure or a Cursor provider error instead of the documented fallback.

title: Cursor Fallback Is Wrong
body: **Cursor Fallback Is Wrong** This still describes the missing-`transport` Cursor behavior incorrectly. When `provider: cursor` omits `transport`, provider creation falls back to API before Cursor rejects it as incompatible; it does not resolve to CLI. A user can follow this reference expecting the local Cursor CLI path, then get an incompatibility failure instead. ```suggestion still report a missing `ai.transport` as incompatible. For `provider: cursor`, omitting `transport` is not a working implicit CLI configuration: provider creation falls back to API before Cursor rejects it as incompatible. Set `transport` explicitly when you need a deterministic transport choice. ```

title: Cursor Transport Fallback
body: **Cursor Transport Fallback** This still describes the missing-`transport` Cursor path incorrectly. Provider creation resolves a missing transport to API for every provider, including Cursor, and Cursor then rejects API because it only supports CLI. With `enabled: true` and `provider: cursor`, omitting `transport` leads to an incompatibility/provider error instead of using the Cursor CLI. ```suggestion provider creation. Diagnostics still report a missing `ai.transport` as incompatible. For `provider: cursor`, set `transport: cli` explicitly; a missing transport does not fall back to CLI. Set `transport` explicitly when you need a deterministic transport choice. ```

title: Cursor Defaults Incorrectly
body: **Cursor Defaults Incorrectly** The example repeats the same wrong Cursor behavior. A missing transport does not default Cursor to CLI; it resolves to API before Cursor rejects it. Readers copying this example with `provider: cursor` can omit the required `transport: cli` and get a runtime or diagnostic failure. ```suggestion # How to invoke the provider. When omitted with enabled: true, # Anthropic/OpenAI check/fix fall back to API. Cursor requires cli explicitly. # Diagnostics treat a missing transport as incompatible. ```

title: Cursor Fallback Is Wrong
body: **Cursor Fallback Is Wrong** This still describes the missing-`transport` Cursor path incorrectly. Provider creation resolves a missing transport to API for every provider, including Cursor, and Cursor then rejects API because it only supports CLI. With `enabled: true` and `provider: cursor`, omitting `transport` leads to a provider error instead of using the Cursor CLI.

title: Cursor Fallback Incorrect
body: **Cursor Fallback Incorrect** This still describes the Cursor missing-`transport` path incorrectly. When `provider: cursor` omits `transport`, provider creation substitutes API before constructing Cursor, and Cursor rejects API because it only supports CLI. A user who follows this text can omit `transport: cli` and get a provider error instead of the documented CLI fallback. ```suggestion does not fall back to CLI in the normal provider factory; Cursor requires `transport: cli` explicitly. Set `transport` explicitly when you need a deterministic transport choice. ```

title: Cursor Transport Fallback
body: **Cursor Transport Fallback** This still describes the Cursor missing-`transport` path incorrectly. When `provider: cursor` omits `transport`, provider creation substitutes API transport before constructing Cursor, and Cursor rejects API because it only supports CLI. A reader can follow this with `enabled: true` and `provider: cursor`, omit `transport: cli`, and get a provider error instead of the documented local Cursor CLI path.
